questions.q: What does staking actually give up in exchange for a reward?
options: Nothing -- staking has no real downside
Liquidity (tokens are locked) and risk (slashing, smart-contract, and price risk)
Only transaction fees
Ownership of the token itself
questions.explain: The reward compensates for giving up liquidity while tokens are locked and for taking on slashing, smart-contract, and token-price risk.

questions.q: A protocol pays 10% APR, compounded daily. What is the resulting APY, per this lesson's formula?
options: Exactly 10.000%
About 20%
About 1.0516%
About 10.516%
questions.explain: APY = (1 + APR/n)^n - 1 with n=365 gives approximately 10.516% -- higher than the simple APR because rewards compound daily.

questions.q: Why do many staking protocols enforce an unbonding/cooldown period before withdrawal?
options: So the system can't be drained instantly during a panic or an attack
To generate extra fee revenue for the protocol
It's a legal requirement in every jurisdiction
It has no real purpose beyond tradition
questions.explain: The cooldown prevents an instant mass exit that could destabilize the protocol during a panic, exploit, or governance attack.

options: A tax the government collects on staking rewards
The fee charged for unstaking early
Protocol-enforced destruction of staked tokens as a penalty, usually for validator misbehavior
A bonus reward for validators who stay online
questions.explain: Slashing permanently destroys a portion of a validator's (and often its delegators') staked tokens as a penalty for actions like double-signing or extended downtime.

questions.q: Using the lesson's simple reward formula, what is the approximate reward for staking 1,000 tokens at a 10% annual rate for 90 days, with no compounding?
options: About 100 tokens
About 24.66 tokens
About 2.74 tokens
About 90 tokens
